title: Real-world safety assessment of Mpox Vaccine in Catalonia: Retrospective Cohort Study of Adverse Events of Special Interest and Breakthrough Infections

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the real-world safety of the Mpox vaccine in Catalonia, Spain, as safety data from Europe remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 8,039 adults in Catalonia who received at least one dose of the MVA-BN vaccine between June 13, 2022, and December 31, 2024, using routinely collected primary care and hospital records.
analysis.methods: The study looked for five prespecified adverse events of special interest within 28 days after each dose and described mpox infections diagnosed after vaccination.
analysis.main_results: Fewer than five cases of pericarditis occurred within 28 days of vaccination, and no other event of special interest was identified in that window. Sixteen participants (0.20%; 95% confidence interval 0.11–0.32%) had a recorded mpox diagnosis after vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide preliminary, region-specific reassurance about the short-term safety of MVA-BN vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform ongoing surveillance and monitoring of Mpox vaccine safety in Europe, particularly in Catalonia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has limited evidence due to few events, lack of an unvaccinated comparison group, and inability to establish causality or vaccine effectiveness.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 8,039 adults in Catalonia, Spain, who received the MVA-BN Mpox vaccine between June 2022 and December 2024. The research aimed to evaluate the vaccine's safety by identifying adverse events of special interest within 28 days of vaccination and describing mpox infections post-vaccination. The results indicated that adverse events were rare, with fewer than five cases of pericarditis observed and no other special interest events identified. Sixteen individuals (0.20%) had mpox diagnoses after vaccination. The study provided preliminary reassurance about the vaccine's short-term safety in the region but highlighted limitations, including the absence of a control group and the inability to establish causality. These findings contribute to understanding vaccine safety in Europe but require further investigation.

title: Respiratory Symptoms in Patients with Mpox: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Monkeypox (Mpox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the mpox virus, which has posed a serious threat to global public health security, especially since the worldwide outbreak in 2022.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We searched PubMed, Embase, and other databases for Mpox studies published up to December 2024. The included studies were observational studies that reported at least one respiratory symptom. We employed the metaprop command in Stata software (Version 12.0) to obtain the pooled prevalence and its 95% confidence interval (CI).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Sore throat is the most prevalent respiratory symptom in Mpox patients, followed by oral lesions, cough, and tonsillar signs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: This analysis aims to estimate the pooled prevalence and explore sources of heterogeneity. Subgroup analysis was performed according to the male proportion and geographic region of the study population, in an effort to identify the source of heterogeneity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to explore potential respiratory transmission modes in mpox patients, the possibility of inducing respiratory diseases in clinical settings, and identify typical respiratory indicators that can aid in early diagnosis. This work will contribute to developing more effective and accurate prevention and control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of respiratory symptoms in Mpox patients and explore sources of heterogeneity. The review included 25 observational studies published up to December 2024, which reported at least one respiratory symptom. The pooled prevalence of sore throat was 18% (95% CI 13%-23%), followed by oral lesions (17%, 95% CI 13%-22%), cough (16%, 95% CI 9%-24%), and tonsillar signs (7%, 95% CI 4%-12%). Subgroup analyses were conducted based on the male proportion and geographic region of the study population to identify potential sources of heterogeneity. The findings suggest that sore throat is the most common respiratory symptom in Mpox patients. The review highlights the need for further research to explore respiratory transmission modes, the risk of respiratory diseases in clinical settings, and the identification of early diagnostic indicators. These insights could aid in developing more effective prevention and control strategies for Mpox.

title: Nationwide genomic surveillance of Mpox clade IIb reveals APOBEC3-driven evolution, terminal deletions, and clade Ib introductions

analysis.research_question_and_background: The 2022–2023 global mpox outbreak highlighted the critical need for robust genomic surveillance capabilities to track mpox virus (MPXV) evolution and transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: From August 2024 to June 2025, we generated 326 high-quality whole genome sequences from residual mpox-positive clinical specimens collected by Labcorp across all 10 US Department of Health and Human Services regions.
analysis.methods: Building upon our established SARS-CoV-2 sequencing infrastructure, we implemented a Molecular Loop ® probe-based long-read sequencing approach using Pacific Biosciences Sequel II technology for comprehensive MPXV genomic surveillance across the United States (US).
analysis.main_results: Our analysis identified two samples containing clade Ib MPXV in January and June 2025 and captured shifting trends in clade IIb diversity, with 12 distinct lineages observed. We also identified multiple instances of large (~ 1.6–17.6 kb) deletions proximal to the inverted terminal repeats in clade IIb genomes. Further, we observed significantly higher APOBEC3-associated SNPs per kilobase ( P < 0.001) in clade IIb genomic variable regions relative to their central conserved region.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: APOBEC3 mutation analysis indicated substantial evidence of human-to-human transmission among both clades.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our integrated nationwide surveillance system facilitates real-time genomic tracking of outbreak evolution, with demonstrated capacity across SARS-CoV-2 and MPXV, positioning this platform for rapid deployment during future pathogen emergence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations or bias that would affect confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study used long-read sequencing to surveil mpox virus evolution and transmission in the US, identifying clade Ib introductions and APOBEC3-driven evolution in clade IIb.

title: Geospatial analysis and predictive modelling of mpox transmission hotspots: a case study of Ogun State, Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox is a recurring public health threat in Nigeria and was re-declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024. Nigeria's Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system operates at the Local Government Area (LGA) level, yet published mpox risk models resolve risk only at state level, forcing uniform deployment across heterogeneous LGAs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study developed and evaluated an LGA-resolution geospatial risk layer for the 20 LGAs of Ogun State and integrated it, as a proof of concept, into a live surveillance platform. State-level records of 40 laboratory-confirmed cases (NCDC, 2022) and 151 suspected cases (Ogun State Ministry of Health, 2022–2024), 191 in total, were spatially disaggregated into 189 pseudo-presence points and modelled with an ensemble of maximum entropy, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting over 100 bootstrap replicates.
analysis.methods: Because the 189 points were disaggregated from aggregate counts rather than individually geolocated, the tiers should be read as a spatial prior for triage rather than as confirmed case locations.
analysis.main_results: Discrimination was good under random hold-out (AUC 0.77; Boyce index 0.99) but fell under spatially blocked cross-validation (AUC 0.57), indicating that the layer is suited to coarse triage between tiers rather than within-tier ranking. Seven LGAs were classified high risk along a central corridor anchored on Abeokuta South and the Ijebu–Remo axis, six medium, and seven low.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The tiered layer was exported as GeoJSON with tier-specific action packages and integrated into the IDS-Master platform as a proof-of-concept pathway from spatial epidemiology to routine public health surveillance. The study provides a method for refining risk assessment at the LGA level, which could improve targeted public health interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform more precise surveillance and response strategies at the local level, enhancing the ability to allocate resources effectively. This approach may serve as a model for other regions with similar epidemiological challenges.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results indicate that the model performs well for coarse triage but may not be reliable for within-tier ranking, suggesting that further refinement and validation are needed. The evidence is moderate as it relies on spatially disaggregated data rather than individual case geolocation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the need for more precise mpox risk assessment at the Local Government Area (LGA) level in Nigeria, where current models operate at the state level. The researchers developed a geospatial risk layer for the 20 LGAs of Ogun State, integrating it into a live surveillance platform as a proof of concept. They used an ensemble of machine learning models to analyze 191 cases, spatially disaggregated into 189 pseudo-presence points. The model showed good discrimination under random hold-out but lower performance under spatially blocked cross-validation, suggesting it is suitable for tiered triage rather than within-tier ranking. Seven LGAs were classified as high risk, six as medium, and seven as low. The findings highlight the potential for refining public health interventions at the local level, though the evidence is moderate due to the reliance on aggregated data rather than individual case locations.

title: Systematic Review of Mpox Outbreaks in Africa: Epidemiology, Transmission Dynamics, and Challenges

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Mpox virus (Orthopoxvirus monkeypox), MPXV clades, and mpox disease. The central question is to synthesize the epidemiology, transmission dynamics, and systemic challenges of Mpox outbreaks across African countries.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies and reports on Mpox epidemiology, case fatality rates, and public health responses were sourced from PubMed and institutional sources such as WHO and Africa CDC. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: WHO reported 7,535 confirmed Mpox cases across Africa from 1 January to 6 October 2024, with 6,169 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Evidence from eastern DRC was consistent with sustained human-to-human transmission of clade Ib. The reviewed reports identified substantial gaps in case detection, diagnostic capacity, and vaccine access.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identified gaps in case detection, diagnostic capacity, and vaccine access. There is no explicit mention of conflicting findings or controversies in the evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening laboratory surveillance, case detection, and equitable vaccine access can support outbreak control. The review highlights the need for improved surveillance and response capacity.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines Mpox outbreaks in Africa, focusing on epidemiology, transmission dynamics, and public health challenges. It synthesizes evidence from six studies published between 2022 and 2024, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. WHO reported 7,535 confirmed cases across Africa, with the majority in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Evidence from eastern DRC indicates sustained human-to-human transmission of clade Ib. The review identifies significant gaps in case detection, diagnostic capacity, and vaccine access. It emphasizes the importance of strengthening surveillance and ensuring equitable vaccine distribution to control outbreaks.

title: An accurate multiplex orthopoxvirus IgG panel for distinguishing vaccinated or exposed individuals from naïve individuals using machine-learning-guided feature selection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a rapid, scalable serology method to distinguish immunologically naive individuals from those with prior OPXV vaccination or exposure, addressing the need for accurate surveillance and outbreak response in the post-smallpox-eradication era.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional analysis included 229 human serum or plasma specimens, categorized as naive (born after 1972), presumed smallpox-vaccinated (born before 1972), or MPXV-exposed/infected.
analysis.methods: Serum specimens were analyzed using partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and Boruta/Random Forest feature selection under stratified nested cross-validation.
analysis.main_results: The 11-antigen profile broadly separated naive specimens from presumed smallpox-vaccinated and MPXV-exposed/infected specimens. A five-antigen signature achieved 89.52% overall accuracy and 83.07% balanced accuracy for three-class discrimination and 96.51% overall accuracy with 96.46% balanced accuracy for binary discrimination (naive vs. vaccinated/exposed).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The selected five-antigen profile yielded high binary classification accuracy but did not establish clinical differentiation between vaccination and infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, outbreak response, and vaccine-program evaluation by providing a rapid, scalable serology method to distinguish naive individuals from those with prior OPXV exposure or vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the use of de-identified specimens and the need for further validation in a larger, more diverse population. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a rapid, scalable serology method using machine learning to distinguish between naive individuals and those with prior OPXV exposure or vaccination, achieving high accuracy in a cross-sectional analysis of 229 specimens.

title: A fractional order mpox transmission model with hygiene and vaccination pathways: Analysis and calibration to the 2024 mpox upsurge in the Democratic Republic of the Congo using weekly surveillance data from 2000 to 2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox has emerged as a public health emergency of international concern, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) at the epicentre of sustained clade I transmission and the 2023–2024 clade Ib upsurge.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We develop a seven compartment Caputo fractional order model (SHVEIQR: Susceptible, Hygiene practising, Vaccinated, Exposed, Infectious, Quarantined, Recovered) which couples direct person to person transmission with behavioural and medical intervention pathways.
analysis.methods: We establish well-posedness of the model, derive the control and basic reproduction numbers using the next generation method, and prove local and global asymptotic stability of the disease free equilibrium (DFE).
analysis.main_results: Using publicly reported weekly mpox case counts for the DRC, we calibrate the model to the artefact free accelerating phase of the 2024 upsurge (weeks 9 to 32 of 2024; the 2000 to 2024 series of 1302 weekly observations is used for data description and context, and the calibration window is a 24 week subset of that series).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We show that the memory index systematically delays and flattens the epidemic peak, which combined vaccination and hygiene coverage of roughly 45% in each channel simultaneously pushes the control reproduction number below unity, and that quarantine scale up is, parameter-for-parameter, the single most effective lever available to public health authorities in a low vaccine access setting such as the DRC.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our results provide a transparent, data grounded, and reproducible guide for evaluating mpox control policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A normalized forward sensitivity analysis identifies the transmission rate, quarantine rate, and, at high intervention coverage, the vaccine and hygiene efficacy parameters as the dominant drivers of the reproduction numbers.

analysis.summary_en: This study develops a fractional order mpox transmission model incorporating hygiene and vaccination pathways, calibrated to the 2024 mpox upsurge in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The model, SHVEIQR, couples direct person-to-person transmission with behavioral and medical interventions. The research establishes the well-posedness of the model, derives reproduction numbers, and proves the stability of the disease-free equilibrium. Using weekly surveillance data from 2000 to 2024, the model is calibrated to the accelerating phase of the 2024 outbreak. The findings indicate that the memory index delays and flattens the epidemic peak, and that quarantine scale-up is the most effective control measure in low vaccine access settings. The study highlights the importance of vaccination and hygiene in reducing the reproduction number below unity. However, the fractional order α is not identifiable from the 24-week calibration window and is therefore not estimated. The results offer a reproducible framework for evaluating mpox control policies.

title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impact of mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb on individuals with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), as this population experiences the highest disease burden during mpox outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An extensive autopsy was conducted on a man with advanced HIV-1 who had achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution despite over 6 months of antiretroviral therapy. The study focused on a fatal case of mpox in this individual.
analysis.methods: MPXV DNA was quantified across 76 autopsy samples from various anatomical sites, and replication-competent MPXV was detected in multiple CNS tissues using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. Sequencing of MPXV from body and brain tissues identified widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants.
analysis.main_results: MPXV DNA was found in high quantities in skin and mucosal tissues, while lower levels were observed in CNS tissues. However, replication-competent MPXV was detected in multiple CNS tissues, and neuronal and glial cell infection was confirmed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that replication-competent MPXV and tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates can infect and persist in the CNS of individuals with advanced HIV, highlighting a novel aspect of mpox virus pathogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform future therapeutic strategies for mpox, particularly in immunocompromised individuals, and emphasize the need for targeted interventions in the central nervous system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single case, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the detailed autopsy and molecular analysis of MPXV in multiple tissues.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb on a man with advanced HIV-1, who had achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution. An extensive autopsy was performed, revealing high MPXV DNA levels in skin and mucosal tissues and replication-competent virus in multiple central nervous system (CNS) tissues. Sequencing identified tecovirimat resistance-associated variants, suggesting the virus can infect and persist in the CNS of immunocompromised individuals. The findings highlight the need for targeted therapeutic strategies in such populations. The study's single-case design limits generalizability, but the detailed molecular analysis provides strong evidence of MPXV's ability to affect the CNS in advanced HIV. This case contributes to understanding mpox virus pathogenesis and informs future therapeutic approaches.

title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap

analysis.scope_and_question: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications.

analysis.summary_en: This rapid review examines healthcare workers' (HCWs) preparedness for monkeypox (Mpox) pandemic response in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). It highlights that only 46.8% of HCWs have adequate knowledge about Mpox, despite its high regional case fatality rate. Barriers to preparedness include reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention are associated with higher knowledge levels, but these attitudes do not translate into clinical preparedness, indicating an intention-action gap. The review underscores the need for peer-reviewed information sources and a One Health training framework to address these gaps. The findings suggest a critical need for targeted training and policy interventions to improve HCWs' readiness for Mpox outbreaks in SSA.

title: Accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based nucleic acid detection for Mpox Virus a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Mpox is an emerging and re-emerging infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus (MPXV), posing an ongoing threat to global public health. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) is widely used as the reference method for MPXV nucleic acid detection. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Early, rapid, and accurate detection of MPXV is essential for timely diagnosis, appropriate clinical management, and effective outbreak prevention and control.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based nucleic acid detection methods for the Mpox virus (MPXV). The findings underscore the need for further research to standardize these assays and improve their reliability for outbreak control and point-of-care testing.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the transmission dynamics of monkeypox using a data-driven SEIR model incorporating public awareness and healthcare capacity, addressing the need for understanding disease spread and control strategies during outbreaks.

The model integrates public awareness and healthcare capacity limitations to reflect real-world conditions during outbreaks.
analysis.methods: Model parameters were estimated using demographic and epidemiological data, along with least-squares curve fitting based on reported monkeypox cases in the USA. analysis.main_results: Numerical simulations demonstrated that increased public awareness and timely interventions effectively reduce disease burden and improve outbreak control. title: Rapid Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance Informed Precautionary Public Health Action Following the 2024 Kiteezi Landfill Disaster in Uganda

analysis.research_question_and_background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) has been used to detect pathogen signals during pandemics and mass gatherings, yet its role in sudden-onset environmental disasters remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Following the catastrophic August 9, 2024, Kiteezi landfill collapse in Kampala, Uganda, which caused fatalities, displaced communities, destroyed sanitation infrastructure, and contaminated the surrounding environment with leachate and sewage, the Ministry of Health rapidly deployed WES to assess infectious disease risks and guide emergency public health action.
analysis.methods: Between 10 and 12 August 2024, with sampling initiated within 72 hours of the collapse, we conducted a purposive cross-sectional assessment at five high-risk sites: a leachate-floodwater interface, a flowing leachate stream, two stagnant wastewater pools, and a community borehole. Moore swabs were collected at Sites A-D, and a 500 mL grab sample was collected at Site E. Concentrated extracts were qualitatively tested using commercial qPCR or RT-qPCR assays for selected enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic pathogens. The borehole sample was also cultured for Escherichia coli as an indicator of fecal contamination, and field observations documented potential exposure pathways.
analysis.main_results: Nucleic acids from Shigella spp., Salmonella spp., non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae, enteric adenovirus 40/41, selected enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and rotaviruses A-C were detected in one or more leachate or wastewater samples. We did not detect influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, or mpox virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrated the potential value of integrating environmental surveillance into early disaster-response frameworks. The response team reported implementing precautionary measures, including water-source restrictions, household water treatment, access controls, WASH activities, animal-control measures, and enhanced clinical surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings informed precautionary public health decision-making, including drinking-water protection and exposure-reduction measures. When combined with field observations and routine disaster-response information, these findings supported the operational feasibility of rapid WES deployment in environmental disasters.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The assessment did not establish the effectiveness of these interventions in preventing infections. The evidence is moderate as it is based on qualitative testing and field observations, and the single borehole sample result does not establish water safety.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the role of wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) in assessing infectious disease risks following the 2024 Kiteezi landfill disaster in Uganda. The Ministry of Health deployed WES to detect pathogens in contaminated environments, including leachate and wastewater samples. The study found nucleic acids from several pathogens, including Shigella spp., Salmonella spp., and SARS-CoV-2, but did not detect mpox virus. Field observations identified potential exposure pathways, such as unprotected contact with contaminated water and livestock access to leachate. The findings demonstrated the operational feasibility of WES in disaster response and informed precautionary public health actions, including water-source restrictions and enhanced clinical surveillance. However, the study did not assess the effectiveness of these interventions. The evidence is moderate due to the qualitative nature of the testing and the limited sample size.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mRNA-LNP vaccines have transitioned from a platform without a licensed product to one that is widely used for diseases like Mpox. It highlights the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms of RNA translation and lipid nanoparticle behavior for vaccine development.

The review emphasizes the need to understand RNA translation and lipid nanoparticle behavior for effective vaccine design. The implications for future research include addressing these gaps and improving antigen design for pathogens with complex immunogenic profiles.

The study emphasizes the need for legal and institutional frameworks to ensure that countries are not penalized for reporting outbreaks, and it calls for the development of such structures as peacetime infrastructure. The findings suggest that improving public health diplomacy can enhance regional cooperation and global health security. However, the study is based on an editorial and lacks empirical data, limiting the strength of its conclusions.

title: A Koopman-PINN Framework for Epidemic Models: Parameter Inference and Forecasting

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a novel framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models, addressing the challenge of improving interpretability and predictive stability in such models.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study applied the proposed Koopman-PINN framework to a normalized SEIRSD epidemic model, using synthetic monkeypox data and real-world datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden for the SARS-CoV-2 virus.
analysis.methods: Synthetic trajectories were generated using a structure-preserving, nonstandard finite difference scheme to ensure reliable training data, and the framework was evaluated through numerical results comparing its performance to classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches.
analysis.main_results: Numerical results demonstrated that K-PINN achieved more accurate parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting compared to classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The integration of Koopman operator theory with physics-informed neural networks provides a more interpretable and stable framework for epidemic modeling, offering novel approaches to parameter inference and forecasting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the K-PINN framework can enhance the accuracy of epidemic predictions, which may inform public health strategies for monitoring and controlling mpox outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to synthetic and real-world datasets for SARS-CoV-2 and monkeypox, and the evidence is strong as it directly compares the framework's performance to existing methods using numerical results.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a Koopman-enhanced physics-informed neural network (K-PINN) framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models. The framework integrates Koopman operator theory with physics-informed learning, mapping epidemic states into a latent observable space where dynamics evolve approximately linearly while satisfying governing equations. The method was applied to a normalized SEIRSD model using synthetic monkeypox data and real-world SARS-CoV-2 datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden. Results showed that K-PINN outperformed classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches in parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting. The authors interpret this as a novel and effective machine learning framework for epidemic modeling, with potential implications for public health surveillance and control of mpox outbreaks. The study's evidence is strong, though limited to specific datasets, and the framework's performance is validated through direct numerical comparisons.
